doc.title: Will Shade and Dewey Corley Interview, 1960-05-25

chapter: Beale Street and the early Memphis scene
title: Wagon bands, playing by ear and instrumentation
summary: Bands played blues in wagons; some read music and others played by ear from about 1904-05; typical lineups had no saxophones.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Who played what: early band size and instrumentation

blocks.x: What about the music? Did they have full bands?

Sure, used to hold the band around in the wagon. The county in the wagon, drum, bass, fiddle, everything all in the wagon. WC and we'd play in the Memphis Blues, the St. Louis Blues, Yellow Dog Blues, and all such as that. They wouldn't be out on the street, bailouts and dancing all up on... up and down the street, like that.
Did those bands play with music or not? Would they have the music, sheet music in front of them?
They used to play by music and then again they used to play by ear.
What year did they start playing by ear around here?
Oh, that was around about... around in...
four or five. 1904 and 1905, they were playing by ear then?
How big a band would they have?
They'd have six and eight feet, sometimes five, just a chord note.
Chambon, piano, drums, there wasn't no saxophones in them days. Drums and plankton, banjos and like that. Okay. guitars, violins, so forth.
Did they have a clarinet then? Were they out?
38 clarinet then, they were out. Yeah.
But no saxophones in those days?
No saxophones in them days. The saxophones that came in here a few years back. Oh, that's right.
